references.text: John 12:39 quoted directly from Isaiah 6:9-10 to explain why people could not believe, as the apostle referred to the prophet's words about the heart being hardened and eyes closed.
In Romans 11:8, Paul quoted Isaiah 6:10 directly to describe God's action of giving a spiritual slumber and closed eyes, which is the same theme John mentions.
Matthew 13:14-15 uses Isaiah 6:9-10 to explain why Jesus spoke in parables, paralleling John's use of the same text to explain the lack of faith.
Luke 8:10 refers to Isaiah 6:9-10 to explain that the mysteries of God's kingdom are given to some, while others see without seeing, a direct link to John's quotation.
Acts 28:26-27 quoted Isaiah 6:9-10 toward the end of the book to conclude that the people could not believe, just as in John 12:39.
